handoff: Approve: all five criteria traced to tests that assert them (AC5 is a doctor integration test, left to CI); test and typecheck green. Two minor notes: max: on a use route also counts non-deriving feeders (D5 reading); agent exit feeders untested.

findings.title: With max: on a use route, non-deriving feeders are counted too
findings.detail:
countExit sets `counted = group.edges` whenever the use route gives max:, so a feeder that derives nothing (for example a check pass or an agent done leaving through the exit) joins the exit counter even when other feeders derive. D5 says 'feeders that derive nothing stay uncounted' and 'with max: they share it' (the deriving feeders), and only 'max: on a use route with no deriving feeder counts every feeder'. The implementer records this as a decision (the flattener copies max onto every feeder edge, so leaving one out would leave a per-edge max in the pin). Defensible, untested either way.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Have the person confirm the reading; if kept, add a sentence to D5 (slice 06's docs) and a test pinning it.

findings.title: Agent feeders of a shared exit have no test
findings.detail:
countExit derives agent send-back feeders together when any one lies on an uncounted loop (derive-counters.ts agentsDerive), a rule the slice's Notes and D5 name, but no test in 'one counter per shared-file exit' covers an agent feeder that derives; the only agent feeder tested (fix.done) is a forward outcome.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Add a test with an agent send-back leaving through an exit routed back into a loop, expecting `<use>.<exit>` max 3.
